test.doc: The headends belong to the provider (ACME Networks, tenant group Service provider); each branch to its customer company (tenant group Customers) with account, industry, tier and contract start as custom fields on the tenant. The branch location carries the street address; router and location carry the ACME design pattern, which is derived from how many tunnels (headends) the branch has: 1 = ACME-SH, 2 = ACME-DH, 3+ = ACME-MH. The portal's Branches page exposes and filters on it.

suite.doc: The IPsec lab as modelled in the shared Nautobot: devices match the routers, p2p links are cabled, the VPN lives in the core VPN app (VPN, tunnels, hub/spoke endpoints, profile with Phase 1/2 policies), eBGP peerings match the live sessions, the rendered NAC device model matches the committed file, Golden Config is compliant.

suite.name: 07 Firewalls

test.doc: The config context sets the remote syslog target (VictoriaLogs on the NMS, UDP 5514); render_vyos pushes it. The kernel's forward-filter lines arrive tagged with the firewall's hostname, the same lines `show log firewall` prints, so the portal's Firewalls tab (source=logs) and the Grafana drops panel / FirewallDropBurst alert see every firewall.

suite.doc: The VyOS firewall in front of each headend: modelled in Nautobot, configured from it, and actually filtering: only IKEv2, ESP and ICMP cross between the spokes and the headend; anything else is dropped.

test.doc: A certificate spoke goes to its pre-shared key through the portal's auth run (its trustpoint retired, its headends keying for it on their PSK profile, SAs on PSK) and back again (enrolled anew, keyring gone, SAs on RSA) — two runs, about ten minutes.

suite.doc: Certificate authentication, chosen per spoke (device ike_authentication, else the lab default): every router with a certificate-authenticated tunnel holds a certificate from the lab CA (pki/ca.py) in the modelled trustpoint, the CA is pinned by fingerprint, those tunnels authenticate with rsa-sig, and a router whose tunnels all use keys holds no trustpoint; Nautobot records what each router presents; the portal renews a certificate and switches a spoke between the two methods.

test.doc: Several run modes save the intent the caller posted, and the portal serialises it through the REST schema — a field the schema does not know is silently dropped and the model loses it (that is how the DCI's NAT and DNS settings disappeared once). Whatever is in lab-intent.json must survive GET /api/intent.

They are wrapped over several lines (every router has a LAN host), so the rewriter has to span lines — this is a dry run of that rewrite on the real lab.conf, read back with bash; lab.conf itself is untouched.

kw.doc: The portal runs one pipeline at a time. When the suites are the `test` step of a run, a portal run this test would start queues behind that very run and never executes — so the test is skipped here and runs when the suite is started from a shell (./lab.sh test) or from a `test`-only run.

test.doc: An extra static route is configured on a spoke by hand. The golden run marks its Static routes feature non-compliant with the `no ...` remediation line; a `remediate` run pushes that line and saves, the next verdict is compliant again, the drift history shows the drift and its repair, and Prometheus (via /metrics) saw the router non-compliant in between.

kw.doc: The portal runs one pipeline at a time. When the suites are the `test` step of a run, a portal run this test would start queues behind that very run and never executes — so the test is skipped here and runs when the suite is started from a shell (./lab.sh test) or from a `test`-only run.

test.doc: Loopback0's description on a spoke is changed by hand (Terraform manages it). A `reapply` run renders the NaC data, plans and applies only that router's resources, and ends with Golden Config compliant; the description is back.

suite.doc: The portal itself: runs queue instead of colliding (one executes at a time, a queued one can be cancelled), every router has a page that gathers its tunnels, authentication, firewall rules, host and runs, and single sign-on (OpenID Connect against the lab's Gitea) is offered and starts a proper authorization-code + PKCE flow.

kw.doc: The management address of any Catalyst 8000v: a headend, a branch, or the DCI chain off west-headend.

kw.name: Run Command
kw.msg:
10.2.0.13# show running-config | section router bgp|route-map|prefix-list
router bgp 65202
 bgp router-id 10.255.1.3
 bgp log-neighbor-changes
 neighbor 172.17.5.1 remote-as 65204
 neighbor 172.17.5.1 description eBGP central-headend (Tunnel5)
 neighbor 172.17.9.1 remote-as 65206
 neighbor 172.17.9.1 description eBGP west-headend (Tunnel9)
 !
 address-family ipv4
  network 10.255.1.3 mask 255.255.255.255
  network 192.168.23.0
  neighbor 172.17.5.1 activate
  neighbor 172.17.5.1 route-map BREAKOUT-central-headend in
  neighbor 172.17.9.1 activate
  neighbor 172.17.9.1 route-map BREAKOUT-west-headend in
 exit-address-family
ip prefix-list DEFAULT-ROUTE description the default route the headends originate (internet breakout)
ip prefix-list DEFAULT-ROUTE seq 5 permit 0.0.0.0/0
route-map BREAKOUT-central-headend permit 10 
 description default route from central-headend (internet breakout; the nearest headend wins on local-preference)
 match ip address prefix-list DEFAULT-ROUTE
 set local-preference 200
route-map BREAKOUT-central-headend permit 20 
 description everything else unchanged
route-map BREAKOUT-west-headend permit 10 
 description default route from west-headend (internet breakout; the nearest headend wins on local-preference)
 match ip address prefix-list DEFAULT-ROUTE
 set local-preference 150
route-map BREAKOUT-west-headend permit 20 
 description everything else unchanged

${out} = router bgp 65202 bgp router-id 10.255.1.3 bgp log-neighbor-changes neighbor 172.17.5.1 remote-as 65204 neighbor 172.17.5.1 description eBGP central-headend (Tunnel5) neighbor 172.17.9.1 remote-as...
kw.doc: Run a show/exec command on a switch over SSH and return its output.

kw.msg: ${run} = router bgp 65202 bgp router-id 10.255.1.3 bgp log-neighbor-changes neighbor 172.17.5.1 remote-as 65204 neighbor 172.17.5.1 description eBGP central-headend (Tunnel5) neighbor 172.17.9.1 remote-as...
kw.doc: Run a show command on a router by name.

test.doc: A branch host breaks out through its nearest headend. A host behind the DCI chain has no breakout preference of its own (its default route comes from the headend over eBGP) — suite 12 checks that path.

suite.doc: Internet breakout: every firewall's uplink sits on the libvirt NAT network and masquerades the site LANs (LAN -> uplink only, replies routed back to the headend), every headend holds a default via its firewall and originates one to its spokes, every spoke prefers the nearest headend's default (local preference from the intent's regions), and every LAN host reaches the internet through its preferred headend — the path shows it and the firewall logs it.

suite.name: 12 Dci

kw.name: Skip If
kw.arg: no DCI chain in this lab
kw.doc: Skips the rest of the current test if the ``condition`` is True.

test.doc: ACME's headend answers for its own zone; the acquisition resolves a name whose A record is an address that exists on both sides, and the DCI's NAT rewrites the answer to the range the acquisition can actually reach.

suite.doc: The DCI chain off west-headend: ACME's data-centre interconnect (DCI) and the acquired company's edge router (ACME-acquisition) behind it. They carry no IPsec — west-headend <-> DCI <-> ACME-acquisition are direct /30 links with plain eBGP — and the acquisition originates its own prefixes (its site LAN and a service prefix on a loopback), which must be routable from every branch over the VPN. Modelled in Nautobot like everything else (devices, cables, prefixes, BGP peerings, tenants) and rendered by the same NaC pipeline and Golden Config template.

suite.stat: c8000v ipsec vti lab.03 Ipsec Vti
c8000v ipsec vti lab.05 Nac Compliance
